text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lingering fuel shortage is a shame for oil-producing Nigeria and buck passing over who is responsible must stop, says the semi-official newspaper in a front-page report.
- National soccer team must beat silly their Guinean counterpart known as Syli Nationale in world cup qualifying match due to be played in Lagos on Saturday.

- The leader of the National Centre Party of Nigeria, Don Etiebet dumps it and joins United Congress Party of Nigeria, which confirms its supremacy by winning run-off polls held on Thursday as it did the local council election last month.
- Crisis in midwestern oil-producing Warri area yet to end as arsonists burn a village in protest over relocation of their local council headquarters.
- Robbers unleash terror on visitors to on-going African trade fair in their hotel in northern Nigerian city of Kaduna, removing cash and property worth five million naira.
- Industries minister Lieutenant-General Mohammed Haladu announces a package of incentives for entrepreneurs who wish to invest in economically disadvantaged areas of the country.
